_doc: CleanupSpec transmission criterion: per (structure, line), the net footprint of squashed speculative loads minus what cleanup undid must be zero — install invalidated (L1D, L2) and spec-evicted victim restored (L1D only). Intra-window churn cancels (net presence, agreed 2026-10-28). cleanup_skip / cleanup_drop never count as undo. Cross-checked by a net-state replay; disagreement is flagged 'inconsistent'. O3PipeView trace only (SimSpect hooks). Evaluated by STAGE3_gem5/check_footprint.py. Scope quotes re-checked against wiki/findings/mdsToRead/FOOTPRINT_DEFENSES_PAPER_AUDIT.md §4, §7 and the PDF text.

requires.why: Cleanup_FOR_L1L2 turns on rand-L2, random L1 replacement and L2 invalidate (Scheme.py:76-82, audit §4C)

claims.quote: CleanupSpec uses randomization for L2/LLC (and for the directory [61]), and consequently only needs to rollback evictions from L1 data caches … CleanupSpec invalidates the line in the L1 cache if it was installed speculatively and fetches the evicted line from L2 cache to restore the original line. For changes to the L2/LLC, CleanupSpec merely invalidates the copy there if it was installed speculatively (as L2/LLC evictions leak no information).

To protect the replacement state, it uses Random Replacement policy for the L1 data cache (any replacement policy can be safely used for a randomized L2 or LLC). For coherence state changes, CleanupSpec delays loads that cause such changes (M/E to S) until they are unsquashable on the correct path.
claims.supports: observation.state = presence; replacement + coherence handled by design (by_design)

claims.quote: We only consider attacks exploiting the data-cache hierarchy, including private data caches (e.g. L1-D cache) and shared caches (L2/LLC) … The adversary may transiently access the cache and modify its state through installs [63], evictions [34], updates to replacement [26] and coherence [62] state.
We deem all transient instructions potentially 'unsafe' until they retire

claims.quote: Changes made to the cache by older non-squashed loads that execute after squashed loads due to re-ordering, need to be preserved and not reversed … corresponding invalidations / restorations are skipped.
the perceived cache state after these operations is as if the transient loads did not access the cache.

spec.text: squashed(i) ∧ lc_seq < i.seq  (pinned 2026-10-28: what the tests realize; i = the event's seq joined to the O3PipeView fetch seqNum; squashed = never retired and younger than a ROB:squash seq while allocated before that squash)

footprint.text: lc_retire < e.tick < fnc_retire (fnc_retire==0 → ∞; no lc annotated → no lower bound) ∧ every annotated unresolved branch still unresolved at e.tick (gem5_common.check_branch_resolutions), same window as check_ld.py

undo.text: cleanup events are matched to squashes by their sq= field

evicted.note: actor = the evict's own seq (the request that caused it)

reported_not_undo.note: a skipped or dropped undo leaves the footprint uncleaned; listed per record

churn.rule: an actor fill of ℓ followed by an actor evict with victim ℓ (before any cleanup) cancels one install and that evict

excluded: L2/DIR fill of ℓ after a cleanup_restore of ℓ in the same undo window (the rollback GETS)
L1D evict inside an undo window whose cause id matches no fill (rollback-space replacement, SIMSPECT_HOOKS.md gaps)
cleanup_side_effects.note: excluded from the count, kept in the net-state replay

balance_scope: all actor fill/evict events in the run (not only those in W), so cleanup of an actor's out-of-window footprint pairs correctly; under-clean is a leak only if the line has ≥1 footprint event in W

leak.text: for each (s, ℓ) ∈ OBS × lines: d_install = installed − churn − invalidated; d_victim = evicted − churn − restored (L1D only). under_clean ⇔ d > 0 ∧ some contributing footprint event of (s,ℓ) ∈ W; over_clean ⇔ d < 0 ∧ the cleanup's squash is a window squash. leak ⇔ ∃ (s,ℓ) : under_clean ∨ over_clean.

cross_check.text: replay fill/evict/inv/cleanup_inv/cleanup_restore per structure to sim end twice: actual (L2 victim removals by actors skipped, benign by design) vs reference (all actor footprint, cleanup and cleanup side-effect events removed). Each differing (s,ℓ) is a net leak unless all its actor footprint is outside W. If the set of leaking (s,ℓ) differs from the count's, the record is flagged inconsistent (pairing/attribution bug in hook or checker) and issued_in_window = count ∨ net (never hide a possible leak).

claim.quote: During cleanup operations (t2 to t3), the process of restoration of cache state does not practically leak information. … Future work can explore making the cleanup-operations incur a constant-time stall to make this theoretically impossible to exploit.
